subject: Re: Ownership handback & feedback license — next steps
messages:
From: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@clientco.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracting@clientco.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClientCo redlines - ownership & training

Hi Hannah / Ben,

Thanks for the call today. We attached the redlined order form. Two primary asks from Legal/Procurement that are blocking signature:

1) Output ownership: ClientCo requires express assignment of rights to outputs produced by the service when generated from ClientCo data & prompts. We need a clear statement that Customer "owns" the output and can productize it.

2) Training / model improvements: ClientCo will not permit use of Customer data or outputs to retrain or otherwise improve Redwood models without explicit opt-in and contractually auditable controls (no telemetry used for model updates).

Please let us know Redwood's proposed contract language and operational controls (isolation, data routing, KMS, proof of non-use). We need these in the next 48 hours to keep our procurement timeline.

Attachments: ClientCo_orderform_redline_20270524.pdf

Best,
Laura Gomez
Head of Procurement, ClientCo

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: ClientCo redlines - ownership & training

Folks — forwarding ClientCo's redlines. High priority: procurement timeline and legal want concrete language we can commit to. Quick notes from the product/ops side:

- Output ownership: Product is comfortable with granting broad usage rights to outputs derived strictly from Customer-provided prompts/data (we already have precedents) but we need to preserve ability to improve models with aggregated non-identifiable telemetry.
- Training opt-in: Engineering can offer an explicit opt-in flag for training, plus a Private deployment option (VPC) for stronger isolation. We can offer an audit statement and KMS integration for key material.
- Operational proofs: we can provide SOC2 evidence and a one-time attestation about non-ingestion of ClientCo data for training for the contract term.

Requesting Legal to propose redline language that: 1) grants Customer output usage rights for their content, 2) carves out model improvement rights for Redwood in a way that preserves aggregated telemetry but not identifiable customer content, and 3) spells out the narrow feedback license (support/bugfix/troubleshooting) with a time/bound and purpose limitation.

Ben — can you take lead on proposed wording for ownership + feedback license? Evelyn / Connor — ops/legal controls + SOC2 attestation. I suggest we draft 2 options (opt-in training vs. default no-training).

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Field Sales (Redwood Inference)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed contract language - ClientCo (draft)

Hi team — draft language attached (redwood_proposed_language_20270526.docx). High level summary of the proposal I plan to share with ClientCo legal:

1) Outputs: "Customer shall own and may use, reproduce, modify, distribute and otherwise exploit all Outputs generated solely from Customer Content and Customer prompts ("Customer Outputs"). Redwood grants to Customer an exclusive, perpetual, transferable right to such Customer Outputs. "

2) Training / Model Improvements: "Redwood shall not use Customer Content, Customer Outputs, or any Customer-provided prompts to train, tune, or otherwise improve Redwood's base models or model weights without Customer's prior written opt-in. Redwood may continue to collect aggregated, de-identified telemetry about service performance and token-level statistics for capacity planning and product improvements, provided such telemetry cannot be used to reconstruct Customer Content."

3) Feedback License (limited): "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, revocable, royalty-free license to use Feedback (as defined) solely to provide the Service, troubleshoot, or address security or reliability issues. Such Feedback license expires 90 days after submission unless Customer provides explicit consent for longer use. Feedback will not be used to train or update model weights absent express opt-in."

Operational commitments to include in the cover letter: Private deployment option, KMS support, SOC2 attestation, and a canary/initial escrow arrangement for first 90 days (we can place telemetry export into an escrow-like mechanism to provide additional assurance).

If no objections, I'll send this to Laura + contracting with an offer to jump on a short legal-to-legal call.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_proposed_language_20270526.docx

From: Miguel Santos <m.santos@clientco.com>
To: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@clientco.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ownership handback & feedback license — next steps

Hi Hannah / Ben — appreciate the fast follow. A few quick points from our side after internal legal review:

- The Outputs language looks promising, but Legal wants clarity on downstream sublicensing and transferability for product features that embed Outputs into combined services. Can Redwood explicitly allow Customer to sublicense downstream in perpetuity?
- The Training carveout sounds acceptable if we can get the written attestation and a technical description of the telemetry that will still be collected.
- The 90-day Feedback license is a good start; can we request a 180-day option for support teams that need a longer troubleshooting window for production incidents?

Let's do the legal-to-legal call Monday morning (ClientCo timezone). Laura will share available times. Please include someone from Engineering who can speak to telemetry detail.

Thanks,
Miguel Santos
General Counsel, ClientCo
